compensating.why: hop 1 creates the builder without namespace awareness
hop 2 hands the children the inherited scope instead of the element's
hop 3 passes a fresh empty scope

edits.old: return owner.createElementNS(namespace == null && colon > 0 ? "" : namespace, tagName);

ownership_reason: Only the gold resolves the namespace of an element: it adds the element's xmlns / xmlns:prefix declarations to the scope, takes the prefix of the tag name, and decides the namespace that the W3C element is created in. Hop 1 creates the document and starts the walk, hop 2 walks the tree and hands each element a copy of the inherited scope (it never adds an entry), hop 3 copies attributes onto the element the gold made, hop 4 passes through. The callers pass the jsoup element itself, so none of them can change the tag name the gold reads, and the scope they pass is documented as the namespace URIs declared by the ancestors; once the gold calls createElementNS with a null namespace and a prefixed name, the W3C DOM throws inside the gold and no caller can recover the element. The gold's javadoc promises the new W3C element in the namespace bound to the prefix; for <fb:like> with no xmlns:fb the variant produces no element (NAMESPACE_ERR). The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling W3CDom.W3CBuilder.head, used in production by the public W3CDom.convert, creates an element whose prefix is not bound with the empty namespace ('doesn't have a real namespace defined'); namespacePreservation, convertsGoogle, simpleConversion, handlesInvalidAttributeNames and convertsGoogleLocation pass through the chain.
